$comment: Brainfood slice contract v1 (plan 8261645, Track C / package C2).
A Brainfood slice is a BOUNDED, derived JSON artifact: a small, auditable
bundle of references plus a fingerprint, never a governed data store.
Bounded means both size and quantity are capped; a slice that exceeds a
cap is split, not truncated in place.
Identity is stable and content-addressed so a slice can be cited by id,
recomputed, and compared without reading its sources again.

authority.note: A slice cites authorities; it never becomes one. Authority membership is the closed set in schemas/decision-b-freeze/jsonb_contract_test.py.

bounds.split_policy: when a cap is exceeded, emit slice.part N/M with parent_slice_id set; never drop refs silently

fingerprint.canonicalization: RFC8785-style canonical JSON of the slice body WITHOUT the `fingerprint` field
fingerprint.rule: a slice whose recomputed fingerprint differs from the stored value is `invalid` and must not be consumed

status_enum.meaning: assembled, not yet fingerprinted/verified; not consumable
fingerprint present and recomputable; consumable as evidence
replaced by a newer slice id; retained for lineage only
retracted by its owner; not consumable, retained for audit
failed fingerprint or bound validation; never consumable

field_contract.slice_version: monotonic integer per logical slice family
field_contract.valid_from: ISO-8601 valid-time start (the world-time the slice describes)
field_contract.valid_until: ISO-8601 valid-time end or null for open
field_contract.recorded_at: ISO-8601 record-time (when this artifact was assembled)
field_contract.source_refs: array of {authority, namespace, record_id, content_hash?} — identity only, no copied source content
field_contract.source_digest: sha256 over the ordered list of source_refs (identity-level)
field_contract.fingerprint: sha256 over the canonical slice body (see fingerprint.canonicalization)
field_contract.interactions: array of vocabulary ids (actors/roles/states/transitions) this slice is about — citation, not assertion
field_contract.bounds_applied: {max_bytes, max_source_refs, max_interactions, max_embedding_refs} actually enforced at assembly time

invariants: A slice never stores source content, only identities and hashes (mirrors resolution.keychain_event_outbox.read_set).
valid_from/recorded_at are both mandatory: a slice without both is `rejected`.
A slice's status is explicit at rest; absence of a status is a defect, not an implied `recorded`.
Reassembling the same sources with the same vocabulary_version yields the same fingerprint (deterministic).
A slice may cite an authority id; it may not claim authority.

example.note: Illustrative shape only. No production slice is emitted by this decomposition.
